subject: science
passage: An insect rarely more than two centimeters ______ bombardier beetle defends itself with a chemical weapon. When threatened, it squeezes two compounds, hydroquinones and hydrogen peroxide, from separate storage sacs into a hardened chamber in its abdomen. There, enzymes trigger a violent reaction that heats the mixture to about the boiling point of water and blasts it out through an opening that the beetle can aim toward an attacker.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "An insect rarely more than two centimeters long" is an introductory phrase that renames the subject, "the bombardier beetle." An introductory element like this is separated from the main clause by a comma.
explanation.A: Correct. The comma separates the introductory phrase from the main clause "the bombardier beetle defends itself with a chemical weapon."
explanation.B: Incorrect. Without a comma, the introductory phrase runs into the subject, and the sentence seems to describe "two centimeters long the bombardier beetle."
explanation.C: Incorrect. A semicolon must join two independent clauses, but "An insect rarely more than two centimeters long" is only a phrase.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A colon must follow a complete independent clause, but "An insect rarely more than two centimeters long" is only a phrase.
